messages:
Maria G: Heads-up — noticed a p99 jump on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate around 14:05 UTC. looks correlated with an increase in fallback routing to the larger quantized variant. anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
Ajay R: Yup saw that too. p50/p95 stable, p99 up ~180ms. Fallback weight to `rlhf-7b-q4` increased around the same time by our autoscaler.
Li Chen: Querying logs now. quick grep: `count by route,variant (requests) | where route=='/v1/generate' and time>now()-15m` — returning ~120k requests, fallback portion jumped from 2% -> 11% at 14:03.
Jordan: Could be KV cache miss amplification for that variant? it has slightly different keying logic. cache-hit-rate in that window?
Li Chen: cache-hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 84% for fallback variant between 14:02-14:06. looks temporally aligned.
Maria G: So hypothesis: fallback weight increased -> more requests hit fallback variant -> variant has lower kvcache hit -> a subset of tails inflate p99. Does that match everyone?
Ajay R: Sounds right. Also check client segmentation — maybe certain tenants routed more to fallback due to quota shaping.
Li Chen: Running breakdown by client tag now. snippet:
```
SELECT client_id, variant, count(*) as cnt, p99(latency) as p99
FROM request_metrics
WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND time> '2025-11-06T14:00:00Z'
GROUP BY client_id, variant
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 25
```
Li Chen: Early results: one mobile client shows 34% of its traffic on fallback and p99 of 420ms there, while others remain ~150-200ms.
Emily S: Ux ask — console shows overall p99 by default. it's hard to tell if spike comes from variant mix vs client skew. We should add a small badge or toggle to split by `variant` and `client` in the latency pane.
Jordan: +1. Also would help to surface cache-hit-rate and fallback-weight on the same timeseries. Right now you have to stitch multiple dashboards.
Ajay R: Quick mitigation: we can temporarily bias routing back to primary for the affected clients if we confirm they disproportionately hit fallback. Also consider raising cold-cache warmup for the quant variant.
Maria G: Agreed. Li — can you confirm whether fallback weight change was automatic from autoscaler or a manual burst?
Li Chen: Looks automated. autoscaler decision log: `decision_id=as-20251106-1402, reason=latency_budget_exceeded, increase_fallback_weight=+9%`. I'll attach the relevant lines to the incident ticket.
Emily S: For the dashboard change, proposal: add a small dropdown to the latency card labeled "group by" with options [route, variant, client_id] and a compact inline checkbox "show routing weights". low-effort front-end, big value.
Maria G: Can we also add a tooltip that explains how p99 is computed across variants (i.e., cohort-level vs global rollup)? People keep assuming it's weighted-mean.
Jordan: Yes, current rollup is global quantile computed over all samples (not weighted means). that's confusing in the presence of a change in variant mix. we should clarify docstring and maybe surface sample counts.
Ajay R: Action items: 1) Li to confirm autoscaler log + identify affected clients (15m). 2) Maria to temporary route-fix plan (15m). 3) Emily to sketch dashboard toggle PR (2d). 4) Jordan to open small telemetry change to surface sample counts and routing-weight timeseries (1d).
Li Chen: Confirmed autoscaler log lines attached. Affected clients: mobile-app-prod (40k reqs), search-plugin (12k). I'll open a repo issue with the per-client breakdown.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: autoscaler decision recorded: as-20251106-1402 applied to pool gpu-pool-3 (see internal link) :white_check_mark:
Maria G: I'll start the routing bias rollback for mobile-app-prod to reduce fallback weight by 7% and watch p99. will report back in 5.
Emily S: adding to backlog: ENG-1298 "latency card: group-by variant/client + show routing weights" — I'll create the ticket and add acceptance criteria.
Jordan: If rollback doesn't help, we should consider a short-term mitigation of increasing quant variant warmup concurrency (so fewer cache misses).
Maria G: rollback applied at 14:18 UTC. initial dashboard check shows p99 falling from 420ms -> 220ms for the mobile client after ~2 minutes.
Ajay R: Nice. keeps global p99 within SLO now. closing incident once Emily's UX ticket lands and Jordan's telemetry PR is merged. :thumbsup:
Maria G: Thanks team — good triage. I'll add notes to the runbook about watchpoints when fallback weight changes.
Emily S: Pull request for ENG-1298 created: https://internal/PR/4321 — small UI, depends on telemetry change.
Jordan: Telemetry PR created: https://internal/PR/4322 — adds sample count and routing_weight timeseries.
Li Chen: Issue with client breakdown: https://tracker/ISSUE-987 — includes CSV export of per-client, per-variant latencies.
Maria G: Great. marking thread resolved for now.
